rgb: This indoor retail scene is beside a glass storefront window with a red sun-and-mountain decal on the left, a white wall and grey doorway frame on the right, and two mannequins placed near the window and wall. Immediately ahead of the camera wearer, approximately 0.4 to 0.8 metres away and within arm's reach, a horizontal black metal clothes rack holding garments on hangers runs from the left toward its right end post. On the far side of the clothes, a woman with glasses stands about 1.2 to 1.5 metres from the camera wearer and can reach the hanging garments, while a striped-sweater mannequin is around 2.5 metres away in front of the window and another mannequin wearing a maroon top and scarf is roughly 2 to 2.5 metres away on the right. The garments and rack substantially block the woman's lower body and portions of the window display, and the right-hand mannequin is partly or entirely cropped by the right edge in frames 1 through 4. Over the five frames, the camera wearer turns their head left in frame 2, revealing the rack's left end with blue clothing and yellow/orange size dividers, the woman, and a second person farther behind on the far left, then turns back right during frames 3 through 5. At the same time, in frames 4 and 5 the woman behind the rack moves rightward toward its end, facing forward and slightly down at the clothes instead of looking directly at the camera wearer.
depth: In all five monocular depth frames, the clothing rack and hanging garments fill the lower foreground as the brightest areas, positioned about 0.4–0.9 m directly ahead of the camera wearer and within arm's reach; meanwhile, a wall column and two mannequins on the right are approximately 1.5–2.5 m away, with about 0.8 m between them. In frames 2, 4, and 5, a glasses-wearing person stands on the left behind the clothes rack, roughly 1.2–1.5 m from the camera wearer and around 0.5 m behind the rack, with the bar and garments hiding them from the shoulders downward. The far-right maroon mannequin is partly clipped by the right edge in frame 1, exits the view in frames 2–4 while the camera pans left and pitches slightly, and returns in frame 5. In frame 2, the person behind the rack faces toward it and slightly right; they vanish below or behind the rack in frame 3, then reappear in frames 4 and 5 looking down at the garments within their reach rather than at the camera wearer. Relative to RGB alone, the depth map distinctly separates the nearby hanging clothes and right-side structural column from the flat storefront-window background, verifying that the red circle and mountain design lie on a distant surface (>3 m) instead of being foreground 3D objects. Nevertheless, depth is unreliable around the frame-2 person, whose head nearly fuses with the dark background depth, over the reflective glass where values flatten to black, and around thin hanger hooks that merge with the rack bar.
segmentation: Against a black, unsegmented foreground and background, the instance-segmentation map extracts mid-ground areas approximately 1.2–2.5 m away, yet repeatedly and severely mislabels retail fixtures and graphics throughout the five frames. In particular, it identifies both the white-and-beige-sweater mannequin, located about 2 m away to the right of the window and facing away and left relative to the camera wearer, and its reflection 0.3 m to the mannequin's left as several overlapping 'person' instances. It likewise calls the second, maroon mannequin on the far right a 'person'; that mannequin is about 1.8 m away, faces forward/left, and is partly outside the right edge in frames 1 and 5. Frames 2 through 5 also incorrectly classify the large red circular design on the background glass, roughly 2.5–3 m away above the clothes rack, as an 'umbrella', while the foreground rack and garments 0.4–0.9 m ahead of the camera wearer and within arm's reach receive no segmentation. The actual person approximately 1.2–1.5 m away behind the rack's left side, who faces the rack and looks down rather than toward the camera wearer and can reach the rack, is broken into incomplete 'person' masks in frames 2 and 5 and entirely omitted in frame 4 because the rack bar heavily occludes them. Although the masks clarify the outline of the far-right mannequin in frames 1 and 5 and follow the background window's horizontal displacement during the camera's left-to-right head turn, the output is highly unreliable: it mistakes mannequins, reflections, and flat wall artwork for people and umbrellas while missing the closest foreground obstructions.
pose: Frames 1, 2, and 5 contain entirely empty pose maps, whereas frames 3 and 4 show only sparse, deformed yellow body-skeleton keypoints in the lower-middle area; no frame contains any detected magenta hand skeletons. The RGB sequence shows a real person behind the clothes rack's left side in frames 2, 4, and 5 at a distance of about 1.2–1.5 m, facing the rack and looking down at clothes they can reach, with the rack at 0.4–0.9 m occluding them below the neck; two mannequins are also positioned 1.8–2.2 m away on the right. Rather than following the real person's head and shoulders on the left, the pose model overlays knotted torso and limb keypoints on foreground sweaters and hangers in frames 3 and 4, about 0.5–0.8 m ahead of the camera wearer and within arm's reach, plus one stray keypoint near the white mannequin on the right. The resulting pose map therefore contributes almost no useful spatial detail, aside from roughly marking lower-foreground areas where garment forms resemble human shoulders as the camera moves. Its performance is highly unreliable across the sequence: severe rack occlusion causes it to miss the genuine person in frames 2, 4, and 5, while it invents body joints on non-living hanging garments in frames 3 and 4.
